statusText:
The CME weekend halt still frames the whole horizon. NQ has not quoted since Friday's 21:00 UTC weekly close and will not quote again until roughly 22:00 UTC on Sunday 16 August, about two hours beyond the end of this 24-hour window. Tail is 12% (low), the action is EA_ON and the status is green, because a pathological one-way price path cannot form while no venue is quoting.

What changed this hour is the shape of the escalation, and it changed in one direction. Iran's deputy foreign minister Kazem Gharibabadi said the Hormuz blockade will continue 'until the US accepts defeat', and Tehran restated that the strait remains under its control after Trump threatened to declare it US territory 'pretty soon'. Until now the unresolved Iran-Oman corridor talks were a live two-sided element; Tehran has effectively removed the near-term reopening path from the table. On the other side, Treasury Secretary Bessent has promised economic measures 'like the world has never seen' next week and Defense Secretary Hegseth says the naval blockade of Iranian ports can be sustained indefinitely by rotating ships. Fortune's read of the menu - secondary sanctions on Chinese purchases, UAE exchange houses, asset confiscation, shadow-fleet infrastructure - notes explicitly that curtailing Iranian barrels removes discounted crude and could lift already elevated oil prices. That is a scheduled, oil-bullish policy catalyst rather than a speculative one, and it is why Stress steps up to 65% (high) rather than holding.

The Lebanon front stayed hot without resolving. Israeli strikes on Deir El Zahrani and Ansar killed at least eleven, the deadliest day since June's ceasefire; Hezbollah promised an 'appropriate' response and urged Beirut to halt 'humiliating' negotiations, while Netanyahu's spokesman framed the strikes as intended to 'jumpstart talks'. Houthi forces hit Mokha with six ballistic missiles, the UAE condemned an Iranian attack on an ADNOC-associated vessel, and Speaker Johnson repeated that the conflict is 'settling soon' - a call he has made since March without it holding.

The hard marks are still Friday's, re-verified this hour: NQ futures 30,141.75 (-0.15%), VIX 14.25 (-2.60%), 10-year 4.696% and 2-year 4.171%, WTI $82.40 (+1.42%) and Brent $88.52 (+1.67%). A 14-handle VIX against crude up 33% on the year remains the central unresolved divergence, and it gets resolved at the reopen, not before.
recommendation: Base strategies stay enabled: Tail 12% maps to EA_ON. There is nothing to trade into and nothing to protect against while the venue is closed - existing-position management, exits and emergency protection remain active as always. Treat Sunday's 22:00 UTC restart as the single checkpoint that matters: it is the first opportunity for two days of one-directional escalation headlines, plus a promised US sanctions package, to be priced at once in a thin auction, and it anchors the danger window rather than any point inside this horizon. This is general market-state analysis for a public dashboard, not personalised financial advice.
headline: Weekend halt holds Tail at 12% and status green, but Tehran rules out reopening Hormuz and Stress steps up to 65% into Sunday's 22:00 UTC restart
body:
Price path: none exists. The entire 24-hour horizon sits inside the CME weekend halt, so there is no session direction, no gap, no retracement structure, no failed pullback and no proximity to extremes to score. Every price input is a Friday close carried forward, which is the correct reason for Tail to be low and the correct reason for Confidence to sit at 65% (solid) rather than higher.

Friday's marks, re-verified from primary sources this hour: NQ futures settled 30,141.75, down 46.75 points or 0.15%, having opened at 30,210.75 and traded a 30,028.50-30,283.00 range on 397,964 contracts against a 52-week span of 22,961.50-30,975.50. That is a consolidation print a fraction below the highs, not a stressed tape.

Cross-asset: VIX closed 14.25, down 2.60%, in a 14.18-14.72 range and near the bottom of its 13.38-35.30 52-week band - equity volatility priced for nothing to happen. The 10-year finished 4.696% (+5.5bp, range 4.625-4.700) and the 2-year 4.171% (+3.1bp, range 4.098-4.178), a roughly 52bp positive spread with no curve signal demanding attention. Crude is the outlier: WTI $82.40 (+1.42%) and Brent $88.52 (+1.67%), up more than 5% on the week, 3.5% on the month and 33% on the year, with the IEA forecasting the widest 2026 supply shortfall in five years. A 14-handle VIX alongside a 33% annual move in crude is the textbook conflicting cross-asset signal, and the contract is explicit that conflicting signals raise Stress rather than Tail.

Geopolitics, the genuinely new material this hour, is one-directional for the first time this weekend. Iran's deputy foreign minister Kazem Gharibabadi said the blockade continues 'until the US accepts defeat' and Tehran restated control of the strait after Trump threatened to declare it US territory 'pretty soon', which Iranian officials called 'delusions'. That closes the corridor-reopening path that previous runs had been carrying as a two-sided element. In parallel the US escalation moved from rhetoric to schedule: Bessent has promised measures 'like the world has never seen' next week, Hegseth says the naval blockade can run indefinitely on ship rotation, and the reported menu - secondary sanctions on entities facilitating Chinese purchases of Iranian crude, UAE exchange houses, confiscation of Iranian state assets under US jurisdiction, and shadow-fleet infrastructure - is explicitly oil-bullish because it removes discounted barrels from the market. Reporting on the exact day of that announcement conflicts, so it is deliberately not entered as a dated calendar event. On the Levant front, Israeli strikes on Deir El Zahrani and Ansar killed at least eleven, the deadliest day since the June ceasefire; Hezbollah promised an 'appropriate' response and told Beirut to stop 'humiliating' negotiations, while Netanyahu's spokesman said the strikes should 'jumpstart talks'. Houthi forces fired six ballistic missiles at Mokha, killing at least three and suspending port operations, and the UAE condemned an Iranian attack on an ADNOC-associated vessel. The only genuine counterweight is Speaker Johnson's 'settling soon' claim.

Why Tail stays at 12%: the definition requires observed persistent directional efficiency, shallow pullbacks, repeated extension after failed retracements or NQ holding near extremes. None can be observed because nothing is quoting, and the contract forbids treating hypothetical post-event alignment as already observed. The one-point increment over the prior hour reflects only that the reopen is an hour nearer and its distribution is wider, not any observed structure. Reopening-gap risk two hours beyond this horizon is not a within-horizon one-way path.

Why Stress steps to 65% (high): three things hardened at once. Tehran explicitly removed near-term Hormuz reopening, the US escalation acquired a schedule and an explicitly oil-bullish transmission channel, and a second military front stayed live with a promised Hezbollah response outstanding. Two full days of that will be repriced in a single illiquid Sunday-evening auction against a VIX that has priced none of it. Stress is the correct home for all of it and it should not decay while it remains ahead.

Why Confidence is 65%: the index level, VIX, both key yields, both crude benchmarks, the geopolitical thread and the seven-day calendar were all read from primary sources this hour and cross-checked. Against that, the newest price evidence is now over 31 hours old with no live path to corroborate it, several sources refused the fetch, and the date of the US sanctions announcement could not be resolved between reports. Solid, not high.

Dominant mode is mixed: escalation dominates the flow but de-escalation claims are still running, oil and equity vol disagree sharply, and there is no tape to arbitrate between them.

lookbackSummary: The last 24 hours contain no tradeable price action: the window opens an hour before Friday's 21:00 UTC weekly close and every slot after that sits inside the CME halt. Claude published 23 of 24 hourly assessments, with only the 20:00 UTC slot on 14 August missing. Tail never left the low band, ranging 2-11%, and EA_ON green held in every published slot. The informative movement is in Stress: it collapsed to 12% in the dead hours immediately after the Friday close, then climbed almost monotonically from 45% at 00:00 UTC to 62% by 19:00 UTC as weekend geopolitical headlines accumulated with no venue to price them. Confidence improved in parallel from 37% overnight to 64% as successive runs verified Friday's closes, the cross-asset picture and the seven-day calendar from primary sources.
outlookSummary: The next 24 hours are entirely inside the CME halt, so the forecast is a headline-accumulation path rather than a price path. Tail stays in the low band throughout, 11-13%, keeping EA_ON and green in every slot, drifting up only fractionally as Sunday's restart approaches. Stress holds 65% through Saturday evening, eases to 62-63% in the overnight dead zone where headline flow historically thins, then rebuilds steadily to 70% across Sunday as the reopen nears and two days of Hormuz, Lebanon and US-sanctions headlines queue up for a single illiquid auction. Confidence dips to 61% overnight on pure staleness - the newest hard marks will be more than 40 hours old by then - and recovers to 67% on Sunday as Gulf shipping activity and any statement on the promised US measures provide the first genuinely new information since Friday. The real checkpoint, the 22:00 UTC Sunday restart, sits about two hours beyond this horizon and is where the danger window is anchored.

forecastDetail.comment: The CME weekend halt owns this slot in full: NQ has not quoted since Friday's 21:00 UTC weekly close and will not quote again until roughly 22:00 UTC on Sunday. No venue is printing, so no persistent directional efficiency, failed pullback or extension can be observed and Tail stays at 12%. Stress steps to 65% (high) because Tehran has now explicitly foreclosed the near-term corridor-reopening path.

Unchanged mechanics. The one thing that can move in this window is headline flow, and the current thread is two-sided: Iran's deputy foreign minister says the blockade runs 'until the US accepts defeat', while Speaker Johnson repeats that the conflict is 'settling soon'. Two-sided flow with no venue to arbitrate is a Stress input, not a Tail input.

Saturday evening in the Gulf and overnight in the US. Newsflow historically thins here, so Stress eases a point to 64% and Confidence slips to 64% purely on the ageing of Friday's marks, which are now more than 31 hours old. Status stays green on Tail 12%.

Deepest part of the weekend dead zone. Tail eases to 11% as the reopen is still more than 22 hours away and nothing in the interim can create a price path. Stress holds at 64%: the Lebanon front and the Hormuz blockade are both unresolved and neither decays overnight.

Sunday begins in Europe with no venue and no new hard data. Confidence drifts to 63% on staleness alone - every price input remains Friday's close. Stress eases to 63% in the quietest window of the horizon, still firmly in the high band because the underlying escalation is intact.

Asian pre-dawn. Any genuinely new information in this slot would come from Gulf shipping activity or an overnight statement on the US measures Bessent has promised for next week. Absent that, Tail holds 11% and green, Stress 63%, and the run rate of the headline queue that Sunday's reopen must absorb continues to build.
